metadata.case_name: GHULAM HUSSAIN v. LAM WAH CHAU AND ANOTHER

injuries.description: multiple pelvic ring fractures and major instability
source: "Mr. Hussain has sustained forceful lateral compression to his pelvis resulting in multiple pelvic ring fractures and major instability. He has required multiple major operations to stabilize the pelvis. Despite a lot of efforts by the surgeons to restore the anatomy, there is still much residual deformity left after the fracture has healed as exemplified on the x-ray and CT scan. The prognosis for this deformity is not good because it is very unlikely that further remodelling or improvement will take place either by natural healing or further surgical procedures."
injuries.icd_description: Fracture of pelvic ring with complete disruption of posterior arch

injuries.description: fracture of his left pubic bone
source: the Plaintiff, who was then aged 27, was admitted to Princess Margaret Hospital, suffering from the following main injuries sustained as a result of the accident: fracture of his left pubic bone; fracture of his right superior and inferior pubic rami; fracture of his right sacral ala; and diastasis i.e. separation of his right sacro-iliac joint.

injuries.icd_description: Dislocation of sacroiliac or sacrococcygeal joint without disruption of pelvic ring

injuries.description: partial damage to the membranous urethra (most probably)
source: "He also had, associated with the pelvic fractures, most probably, partial damage to the membranous urethra, that caused retention of urine and required insertion of indwelling catheter to drain the bladder on admission to the Hospital."

injuries.description: permanent mal-union / mal alignment of the right sacral lliac joint, resulting in a weak right hip
source: "As the result of the crush injury to his pelvis on the 27th May 1999, Mr. Hussain suffered from multiple fractures of his pelvic, resulting in a disrupted, unstable pelvic ring. This required a series of orthopaedic operations, and eventually healed up with permanent mal-union / mal alignment of the right sacral lliac joint, thus resulting in a weak right hip."

injuries.description: neurogenic damage to the innervation of the genitalia
injuries.body_part: innervation of the genitalia / pelvic nerves
source: "Both of them are related to the fracture of the pelvis from neurogenic damage to the innervation of the genitalia."
injuries.icd_description: Injury of peripheral nerve of abdomen, lower back or pelvis

manifestations.description: unable to pass urine on admission (required Foley catheter insertion)
mild degree of painful sensation at the right side of his penis
persistent numbness / paraesthesia of the right side of the penis
mild to moderate impairment of erectile function as compared with pre-accident (able to have sex 2-3 times a week but quality and duration much reduced)
required temporary use of crutches after discharge; later could walk unaided by 11 September 2000

treatments_received: Foley catheter insertion (catheter removed on 2 June 1999)
temporary skeletal traction of right lower limb (29 May 1999)
open reduction and sacral bar insertion (1 June 1999)
removal of the external pelvic fixator (15 July 1999)
treatments_future: oral erectogenic medication (Viagra), 50 mg taken one hour prior to intercourse, assessed yearly for continued need

losses.description: Residual deformity of pelvic ring, permanent mal-union / mal alignment of the right sacro-iliac joint resulting in a weak right hip; partial damage to membranous urethra with initial urinary retention

losses.category: Loss of sexual function and sexual life
losses.description: persistent numbness/paraesthesia of the right side of the penis and mild to moderate impairment of erectile function with reduced quality and duration of intercourse
